description: US-23 How far through the group we are, and who is still missing — /ausgabe states 'Gruppe Rot: 34 von 61 Haushalten abgeholt' as one line and folds the group's list behind it. Opening the list shows every household of today's group in customer-number order with the served ones marked; clicking a name looks that household up, which is the same act as typing their number. Everything is DERIVED from today's distribution records on every read — no stored counter, no schema change and no migration. The ONE new port method is DistributionRecordRepository.listForDay. Requires batch 22 (US-21) to be MERGED first: this batch EXTENDS src/application/distribution/read-group-roster.ts and edits the same screen. Source: tasks/prd-us-23-group-progress.md

userStories.title: groupProgress — how many of a roster collected today (domain)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one pure rule for the tally, so the number in the summary and the marks in the list can never tell different stories. Source: tasks/prd-us-23-group-progress.md §US-023.1
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/domain/distribution/groupProgress.ts exporting groupProgress(entries: ReadonlyArray<ProgressEntry>): Progress, with ProgressEntry = { readonly blocked: boolean; readonly servedToday: boolean } and Progress = { readonly served: number; readonly expected: number }
served counts every entry with servedToday

expected counts every entry that is NOT blocked, PLUS every blocked entry that has servedToday. A blocked household cannot collect (US-08), so counting it in the denominator would put the tally permanently out of reach; but a household blocked AFTER they collected this morning did collect, and dropping them from the denominator alone would make served exceed expected
The invariant served <= expected holds for every combination of the two flags, with a NAMED test that says so
An empty roster gives { served: 0, expected: 0 }

STRICT TDD: the invariant-breaking test is written FIRST, red before green. Named tests: nobody served; everybody served; a blocked household is not expected; a blocked household who was served counts in both; the invariant across all four flag combinations
The module is pure: no I/O, no Date, no import from Next.js, React or Prisma
Domain coverage stays at 100%: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes

userStories.title: listForDay — every hand-out written on one Berlin day (ports + infrastructure)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the day's records in one query, because the roster is ~120 households and one query per household would make the counter's main screen the slowest in the app. Source: tasks/prd-us-23-group-progress.md §US-023.2
acceptanceCriteria: DistributionRecordRepository in src/application/ports.ts gains listForDay(dayKey: string): Promise<ReadonlyArray<DistributionRecord>>, documented in the file's voice

The parameter is a BERLIN day key as berlinDayKey writes it (YYYY-MM-DD) — the same notion of 'the same day' the once-per-day rule and the unique constraint already use. The adapter must NOT re-derive a day from an instant

The adapter in src/infrastructure/prisma/distribution-record-repository.ts implements it as a SINGLE findMany({ where: { dayKey } }), mapped through the existing toRecord, so the dayKey column still never leaves the adapter

Thin integration test against a throwaway SQLite file, following the patterns already in distribution-record-repository.test.ts: records on the asked-for day are returned; records on the day before and the day after are not; an empty day returns []
NO schema change and NO migration. The table has no index on dayKey alone and does not need one at roughly 240 rows a week — adding one is a decision for the day a measurement asks for it
The existing listForCustomer, findById, create, setPaid and remove are untouched
Test data is synthetic (Faker); no real names
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
npm run test:coverage passes (domain and application stay at 100%)

userStories.title: The roster carries who they are and whether they collected (application)
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want one read to answer who is in today's group and which of them have been served, so the screen shows one consistent picture of the afternoon. Source: tasks/prd-us-23-group-progress.md §US-023.3
acceptanceCriteria: readGroupRoster in src/application/distribution/read-group-roster.ts is EXTENDED — not replaced, not renamed, not copied into a second use case. GroupRosterView gains members and progress

members is ReadonlyArray<GroupRosterMember> with { customerId, customerNumber, firstName, lastName, blocked, servedToday }, in the order the repository answered — lowest customer number first. Nothing here re-sorts it

servedToday is true when the day's records hold one for that customer, read through ONE call to listForDay(berlinDayKey(deps.clock.now())) and joined by customerId in memory. NEVER one query per member
The join is by customerId, the surrogate id — never by the customer number, which is a reusable slot attribute
progress is groupProgress(members) from US-001 — the tally is not counted a second time here
previous, next, group and isEmpty keep the meanings US-21 gave them, and US-21's existing tests keep passing UNCHANGED
The use case still WRITES NOTHING: no audit entry, no status change, no record

TDD against HAND-WRITTEN FAKES. Named tests: a member with a record today is served; a member with a record from yesterday is not; a member with no record is not; the day compared is the BERLIN day, tested at 23:30 Berlin on a day whose UTC date is already the next one; a blocked member appears in members and not in expected; records belonging to customers of the OTHER group are ignored
Time comes from the Clock port — no zero-argument new Date()
Application coverage stays at 100%: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes

userStories.title: The tally, and the group list behind it (presentation)
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to see how far through the group we are, and to open the list to find who is still missing and call them up. Source: tasks/prd-us-23-group-progress.md §US-023.4
acceptanceCriteria: /ausgabe renders a Card BETWEEN the banner and the counter card, holding a <details>/<summary> disclosure that renders CLOSED

The summary is ONE line naming the group in words, the number served and the total, with data-testid="group-progress" on the element holding exactly that sentence — the two figures stay in ONE node so a screen reader does not announce them as unrelated fragments
Closed, the card is <= 80px tall measured at 1440x900. It sits above the counter, so every pixel it takes is a pixel the verdict loses — put the measured number in the commit message

Opening it reveals the group's households in customer-number order, each row carrying the customer number, the household's name, and — when served — the word 'abgeholt' in a <span data-testid="served-<customerNumber>">
The served mark is a WORD. Any icon beside it (lucide Check) is aria-hidden. A tick alone is chrome, and chrome never travels without the word (US-03.4, ui_conversion_guide rule 9)
ONLY the served rows are marked. The unserved are the default state and get the name and nothing else — 'chrome marks the exception', docs/ui_conversion_guide.md

A blocked household's row says 'gesperrt', rendered the way /kunden already says it (the StateWord pattern in src/app/kunden/page.tsx) rather than with a new treatment. Do NOT paint the rows with the group tint — the banner directly above already carries it

Each row's name is a <Link href="/ausgabe?nummer=<customerNumber>">, so clicking it looks that household up on this screen exactly as typing the number would, and the disclosure comes back CLOSED on the new page load
The list scrolls inside its own container (max-h-* plus overflow-y-auto) rather than pushing the counter down the page
The list is laid out in columns at wide widths (e.g. sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3) so a group of ~120 is scannable, and stacks below sm
An empty group states so in words instead of rendering an empty disclosure
Every German string is a new key under de.distribution.progress in src/i18n/de.ts — no German literal in the component

The page stays a SERVER component and the disclosure stays <details>: NOT Dialog and NOT client state. At the counter the queue is waiting, so nothing may have to be dismissed before the next customer is served (ui_conversion_guide rule 4)
document.documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth is 0 at 1920, 1280, 1024, 800 and 390
Customer numbers use tabular-nums so the column of numbers reads as a column
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
Full e2e suite passes: npm run test:e2e (rebuild and pkill -f next-server first)

Verify in browser using the playwright-cli skill against a PRODUCTION build, reading the ACCESSIBILITY SNAPSHOT: the summary is announced as one full sentence, each row's link is named with the number and the name, and each served row announces the word
